column1: # Formation energies the vendored tables DO carry and that must not be used anyway.
# This is a different fact from "no energy", and the whole point of the file is that the
# two must not report as the same thing. A missing energy is a coverage or a naming gap and
# is fixed by supplying an identifier. An energy listed here EXISTS, resolves, and has a
# quoted uncertainty -- and the quoted uncertainty is refuted by evidence outside the
# estimator that quoted it. The number is not a smaller number; it is not a number.
# any step with a listed participant as `cannot_say` with reason `refuted_uncertainty`,
# carrying dGr'0 in the report so a reader can see what was withheld and why.
# NOTHING HERE IS A CORRECTED NUMBER. A row records that a disagreement was measured, not
# what the right value is; there is no column for one, deliberately. What would remove a
# row is a MEASURED formation energy, not a third extrapolation.
# AUTHORED HERE, NOT DOWNLOADED -- resolved against the repository rather than through
# YSTWIN_THERMO, for the same reason as heterologous_metabolites.tsv.

column3: REFUSES A MAGNITUDE, NOT A VERDICT -- see below. Both available estimators are extrapolations and they do not agree on how large these energies are. Across the three steps of data/pathways/beta_carotene.toml the ModelSEED group-contribution and eQuilibrator component-contribution standard energies differ by 22, 96 and 124 kJ/mol against quoted errors of 4.9, 17.4 and 15.5 -- 4.5 to 8.0 times apart. The disagreement is NOT specific to C40 polyenes, which is what this row used to claim: CRTE, which touches no C40 species at all, disagrees by 8.6x, the largest ratio of the four. Whatever the two methods disagree about, it is prenyl chemistry generally and not eleven conjugated double bonds. WHAT THEY DO AGREE ON IS THE SIGN, every step, by more than they disagree with each other, so bridge/equilibrator.py::PreferredEnergies.both_dg0 reports the feasibility verdict as robust and pathway/thermo_gate.py returns it. A single estimator cannot check this and still yields cannot_say. HISTORY: 91/275/252 kJ/mol at 16-22x until the kcal/kJ unit error in bridge/thermodynamic.py was corrected on 2026-08-30, then 22/225/124 with CRTI straddling zero -- which was fba/carotenoid.py writing CrtI with four free FAD as terminal acceptor, thermodynamically impossible at +166 kJ/mol on a step Verwaal 2007 runs to completion. Written as the flavin oxidase it is, the sign disagreement is gone. Two modelling errors of ours, one after another, were being reported as uncertainty in the literature.
